Frame houses and greystone two-flats in the west, Wrigley Field and three-flats in the middle, and courtyard buildings and high-rises toward the lake.

districts.name: West Lakeview and Southport
districts.intro: From Racine Ave west to Ravenswood Ave, Diversey to Irving Park: frame houses, greystone two-flats and newer four-storey condo buildings, with shops along Southport Ave and Lincoln Ave.
districts.work: Service and meter upgrades in two- and three-flats, de-conversions back to single-family houses, and garage EV chargers. The largest share of our Lakeview permits is here.

districts.name: Graceland West
districts.intro: The blocks north of Irving Park Rd up to Montrose Ave, between Ravenswood Ave and Graceland Cemetery: Berteau, Cuyler, Belle Plaine and Hutchinson.
districts.work: New meter banks for apartment buildings, two-unit rehabs, house additions and garage subpanels. Our record here includes a 19-meter, 1,200-amp service on W Berteau.

districts.name: Wrigleyville
districts.intro: Around Wrigley Field, Clark St and Addison St, from Cornelia up to Irving Park: brick two- and three-flats, the row houses of Alta Vista Terrace and the bars along Clark.
districts.work: Older multi-unit services, bar and restaurant power, and jobs planned around night games, when the streets from Belmont to Irving Park become a tow zone.

districts.name: Central Lakeview
districts.intro: Diversey to Cornelia between Racine and Halsted: the Belmont 'L' station, the landmark three-flats of Newport Ave and Terra Cotta Row on Oakdale Ave.
districts.work: Vintage three-flats and courtyard condos, coach houses, shop and daycare build-outs on Belmont Ave, and Landmarks review for exterior changes on landmark blocks.

districts.name: Northalsted
districts.intro: The Halsted St and Broadway corridor from Wellington to Irving Park, with the Rainbow Pylons on Halsted, bars and restaurants at street level and walk-ups behind.
districts.work: Restaurant and bar fit-outs, three-phase services, and condo buildings with garages getting EV chargers. Our record includes restaurant work on N Halsted and N Broadway.

districts.name: East Lakeview
districts.intro: East of Broadway to Lake Shore Dr and Belmont Harbor: high-rise condos, 1920s courtyard buildings, and the Hawthorne Place and Surf-Pine Grove landmark districts.
districts.work: Unit panels, kitchen circuits and lighting in towers under building management rules, and new services and unit renovations in older apartment buildings on W Roscoe St and W Belmont Ave.

buildings.title: Two-flat or three-flat

buildings.changes: Two- and three-flats here usually share one service, with the meters and panels together in the basement. Many still have 100-amp services, and laundry, air conditioning or an EV charger can mean a new service with a meter for each unit.

scope_lede: The same job on paper can cost very differently in a West Lakeview two-flat, a courtyard condo on Surf St and a Lake Shore Drive tower. These are the things that change it, and most are settled at the walkthrough.
scope_rows: Alta Vista Terrace, Hawthorne Place, Newport Avenue, Surf-Pine Grove and Terra Cotta Row are Chicago Landmark districts. The Commission on Chicago Landmarks reviews permits there, mainly for street-facing changes such as a service mast, a moved meter or facade lighting.
Many two-, three- and multi-flats still run on 100-amp services. A new service with a meter and panel for each unit needs a ComEd appointment as well as a City permit.
Older houses and flats can still have fuse boxes or cloth-covered wire, and opening a wall can show more original wiring than expected.
Fishing wire through plaster and lath in Lakeview's frame houses and vintage walk-ups is slower than drywall and needs careful patching.
Courtyard buildings, walk-up condos and towers usually want a written proposal and a certificate of insurance before work in units or common areas.
Lakefront towers book freight elevator time, set working hours and limit where boxes can go in concrete slabs.
Permit Parking Zone 383, from Belmont to Irving Park and Broadway to Ashland, is a tow zone from 5pm to 10pm on night games, and Addison can close around games.
A rear coach house or garage is fed from the front building. A new feed, subpanel or EV charger can mean new conduit along the gangway or across the yard.
Many stand-alone electrical jobs go through the City's Express Permit Program. Renovations, de-conversions and build-outs need plans and a standard review.
Signs are permitted separately from the electrical work, so a bar or shop refit may need two permits.
Bars and restaurants on Clark, Halsted and Broadway often need work before opening, so agree the hours before the job is scheduled.
hourly_answer: We quote by scope, not by the hour, because the hours on a Lakeview job depend on the factors below. Replacing a 100-amp service in a West Lakeview two-flat and adding a circuit in a Lake Shore Drive tower aren't the same kind of day. The written quote tells you the whole price before you agree to it.
choosing_building_why: Lakeview changes block by block: frame houses and greystone two-flats in the west, three-flats around Wrigley Field, courtyard buildings and towers toward the lake.
choosing_building_answer: In Lakeview, 79 City permits since 2012: meter-bank service upgrades in two-flats and apartment buildings, panels in Lake Shore Drive high-rise units, new four-storey condo buildings, restaurant and daycare build-outs, and a row house on Alta Vista Terrace
choosing_paperwork_why: Lakefront towers and condo associations want a certificate of insurance and a written proposal, and five landmark districts add review of exterior changes.
where_we_fit: Highlights is a family-owned contractor based up Lincoln Ave at 5766 N Lincoln. In Lakeview we're the right call for two- and three-flat service upgrades, condo and high-rise unit work, older houses and coach houses, EV chargers, and bar, restaurant and shop fit-outs. Base-building work on a lakefront tower, including its fire alarm and life-safety systems, belongs to the building's own contractors, and we'll tell you so.

honest_context: We're a north-side shop. Most of our roughly 1,200 Chicago permits are in Wards 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27. The 32nd and 47th take in parts of Lakeview, but most of it is in the 44th, so this is a steady record rather than our busiest area: about 80 permits since 2012, 11 of them in 2025 and 2026.

Lakeview's electrical work is spread thinly: about 1,170 electrical permits in the last two years among some 340 contractors. The largest categories are work inside individual units, lighting and outlets, followed by build-outs and storefront signs. Our own Lakeview record leans toward service and meter upgrades in multi-unit buildings.

faq: Do I need Landmarks approval for electrical work in a Lakeview landmark district?

Lakeview has five Chicago Landmark districts: Alta Vista Terrace, Hawthorne Place, Newport Avenue, Surf-Pine Grove and Terra Cotta Row on Oakdale Ave. The Commission on Chicago Landmarks reviews permits there as part of the normal building permit, mainly for changes to street-facing elevations, such as a service mast, a moved meter or facade lighting. No separate permit is needed, and our record includes a row house renovation on Alta Vista Terrace.
Can you upgrade the service in my Lakeview two-flat or apartment building?

Yes. New services with a meter and panel for each unit are a large part of our Lakeview record, from four-unit buildings on N Bosworth Ave and W Eddy St to a 19-meter, 1,200-amp service on W Berteau Ave. We pull the City permit and coordinate the ComEd work.
Do you work in Lake Shore Drive high-rises?

Yes. Our Lakeview record includes panel replacements and new kitchen circuits in units on the 3600 block of N Lake Shore Dr, lighting in a unit on the 3900 block and an alteration in a 44-storey condo building on the 2800 block. We work to the building's rules: a certificate of insurance, an elevator booking and set hours.
Can you work in Wrigleyville on a game day?

Yes, but we plan for it. Permit Parking Zone 383, from Belmont to Irving Park and Broadway to Ashland, is a tow zone from 5pm to 10pm on night games, and Addison between Racine and Halsted can be closed around games, so we book Wrigleyville jobs around the Cubs schedule where we can.
Can you power a coach house or detached garage?

Yes. A coach house or garage is fed from the front building, so we check the service first, then run the feed and add a subpanel if it's needed. Our Lakeview record includes coach house rehabs on N Racine Ave and W Roscoe St, a garage subpanel on W Cuyler Ave and an EV charger in a garage on N Lincoln Ave.
Which Lakeview ZIP codes do you cover?
All of Lakeview: 60657 and 60613, from Diversey Pkwy up to Irving Park Rd and Montrose Ave, along with every other Chicago neighbourhood.

service_overrides.Restaurant and bar electrical: Bars and restaurants on Clark, Halsted, Broadway and Sheridan Rd. Our Lakeview record includes restaurant work on N Halsted, N Broadway and N Sheridan Rd.
service_overrides.Tenant build-outs: Shops, studios and daycare centres. We've wired several build-outs on W Belmont Ave.
